mappedContracts.statement: Migrate every direct dependency to the newest maintained upstream release available at execution time, preferring an official next, canary, nightly, dev, beta, rc, or alpha channel over latest stable when such a channel exists and represents newer supported code.
acceptanceCriteria: Codex queries npm dist-tags, publication times, upstream release notes, migration guides, and security advisories at execution time.
Every direct dependency is pinned to an exact resolved version; no caret, tilde, wildcard, floating tag, or floating Git reference remains.
If no maintained prerelease exists, use the newest stable release.
If an unpublished upstream commit is required, pin an exact commit SHA, preserve licence/provenance, and bundle or vendor it so the published npm artefact installs without Git.
The package lock is regenerated and committed.

mappedContracts.statement: Keep tightly coupled dependency families on coherent versions and eliminate accidental duplicate majors.
acceptanceCriteria: All Tiptap packages resolve to one coherent frontier version unless an approved ADR documents an unavoidable split.
Vitest and its coverage provider are aligned.
MCP v2 packages and extensions are aligned.
OpenTelemetry packages are aligned.
npm dedupe and a duplicate-major policy check pass.

mappedContracts.statement: Remove the public package's file:vendor/substack-api dependency and establish a publishable, reproducible ownership model.
acceptanceCriteria: Use an internal workspace package bundled into the tarball, ordinary internal imports, or a separately versioned package.
The clean packed artefact installs without repository-relative files or nested source-tree assumptions.
Vendored source provenance, licence, update process, and divergence are documented.

mappedContracts.statement: Produce installable npm, MCPB, Docker/OCI, stdio, and Streamable HTTP distributions from one reproducible release.
acceptanceCriteria: Clean-room installation and Inspector tests pass for every format.
Registry metadata versions match package and release versions.
No distribution includes secrets, local state, capture artefacts, or repository-relative dependencies.

mappedContracts.statement: Provide one deterministic verification command that runs contracts, generation drift, types, lint, tests, coverage, mutation, fuzz smoke, package checks, MCP conformance, security checks, and receipt generation.
acceptanceCriteria: The command works locally and in CI.
It emits a machine-readable verification receipt conforming to repository-standards.
Release consumes the same verified artefacts rather than rebuilding differently.

mappedContracts.statement: Implement mature supply-chain controls: immutable action SHAs, CodeQL, dependency review, actionlint, zizmor, OpenSSF Scorecard, maintained secret scanning, OSV scanning, licence policy, npm signature audit, SBOMs, provenance, and signed attestations.
acceptanceCriteria: All applicable checks are required and least-privilege.
The bespoke secret scanner is removed or reduced to synthetic project-specific policy on top of a maintained scanner.
SPDX and CycloneDX SBOMs preserve unique package identities and dependency relationships.

mappedContracts.statement: Use trusted publishing, reproducible artefacts, provenance, clean-room installation, version synchronization, release notes, rollback, and staged release channels.
acceptanceCriteria: Long-lived npm publishing tokens are removed after OIDC trusted publishing is verified.
The exact tested tarball is published.
Tags, package metadata, registry metadata, SBOMs, MCPB, OCI image, and GitHub Release use one version.
